newsitem.title: USA: PJM agrees to revise power pool restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: PJM agrees to revise power pool restructuring plan.

text.p: Members of the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) power pool said Thursday they had agreed to revise their restructuring plan as called for by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
The commission Wednesday ordered the 10 utilities in the power pool, which had submitted two competing proposals for setting up an independent operator to come up with a single, improved plan.

"We agreed to incorporate the guidance included in the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's November 13 order in a revised restructuring proposal to be submitted by the end of this year," said Andrew Williams, group vice president of Potomac Electric Power Co, in a statement for PJM.

Pool members bowed to the commission's criticism that the board of directors for their proposed independent system operator was skewed in favor of the utilities at the expense of their potential competitors.
"The members remain committed to incorporate an Independent System Operator which satisfies the Commission's expanded guidance on ISO principles," Williams said.

Competing PJM plans were submitted by PECO Energy Co and the nine other utilities in the pool -- Atlantic Energy Inc, Baltimore Gas and Electric, Delmarva Power and Light Co, PP&L Resources Inc, Potomac Electric Power Co, Public Service Enterprise Group Inc, and three GPU Inc utilities.
